title: Dispatch: Sol review repairs batch B, accounting/projection/limits (attempt 1)
description:
Repair batch B for the integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8: findings S6, S7, S8, S9, S10, S12, S14, S15 from the Sol review bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1 (run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1` and read each finding in full — each has a reproduced failure scenario). A parallel child (batch A) owns the combatant lifecycle: DO NOT edit encounterCombatants.ts, actionEconomy.ts, toolRecordDeathSave.ts, toolStabilizeCharacter.ts, toolSetSuffocation.ts, toolUpdateCombatant.ts, toolBeginTurn.ts, toolStartEncounter.ts, encounterCombatants.test.ts, or actionEconomy.test.ts. No new migration (0036 is the last). Read AGENTS.md and docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendments A3-A5 first.

SUPERVISOR DECISIONS (implement exactly):
S6 (ammunition reservation): a dropped inventory row referenced by an ammunition_expenditure with status 'expended' is reserved for recover_ammunition. claimItem (state/domainMutations.ts) and every other custody path that can take an unheld dropped row (grep: claim, transfer, adopt, reacquire, give) refuse it with an error naming recover_ammunition. Destroying it in place stays allowed (it then counts as moved away). recoverAmmunition marks its expenditures resolved BEFORE it calls claimItem in the same transaction so its own claim passes. Update the claim_item and list_nearby_items descriptions (contract only) if they present such rows as claimable. Update the existing ammunition test at ammunition.test.ts that authorizes an early claim so it now asserts the refusal, and add: repeated expenditure cannot make two expenditure rows alias one physical row; total returned to custody never exceeds floor(expended/2).
S7 (long rest): in rest.ts, apply the exhaustion reduction BEFORE the HP restoration of a qualifying long rest, in the same transaction, and compute/report HP against the resulting effective maximum. Test exhaustion 3/4/5 with and without food/drink: current HP equals the final effective maximum.
S8 (level-up): levelUpEngine.ts projectToLiveCharacter (and any initialization/projection path that writes hp_current from a sheet maximum) keeps hp_max as the sheet value but clamps hp_current to effectiveHpMax(hp_max, conditions). Test progression at exhaustion below 4 and at 4+, with odd and even maxima.
S9 (party roster): party.ts PartyMember.hpMax is the effective maximum (effectiveHpMax with the member's validated conditions), consistent with the acting-character snapshot. One shared-data test with an exhausted non-acting member.
S10 (retained-check visibility): the assembled DM context (contextAssembler.ts, its snapshot type, and the rendered message) lists ACTIVE retained checks for the campaign: retainedCheckId, label, participant (kind/ref), combat instance if any, and visibility — never the total (the total stays engine-owned). Ended checks are omitted. Bound the list (e.g. most recent 20, stated in the rendering). Test: create a check, assemble a fresh context, resolve the original id from it without another hider roll; ended check absent.
S12 (known limits, R0 re-derivation): retire the rule:food, rule:water, and rule:speed entries (add_condition now refuses exhaustion and names adjust_exhaustion, so no trap remains; tool-contract knowledge lives in adjust_exhaustion's description) and delete the now-unused exhaustionLevelLimit helper. Re-derive rule:surprise as a trap statement (resolve_check and resolve_contest cannot determine surprise because each roll would be compared once against one target and fresh rolls replace the hider's check; surprise comes only from passive comparisons recorded by resolve_retained_check and passed to set_surprised) — no step-by-step recipe beyond naming those tools. Fix rule:suffocating's timing: breath running out starts the survival interval (calc suffocation_survival_rounds); the drop to 0 hit points (set_suffocation event drop) happens at the start of the creature's turn after that interval, not when breath runs out. Keep participants valid (each named tool listed and present in the statement). Update ruleAwareness.test.ts / tools.test.ts / ruleDispositions.test.ts assertions accordingly (replace, do not just delete; keep a regression that no limit suggests remove_condition + re-add; add a source-backed timing assertion for suffocation). Update the design doc A5 table rows for these keys ("retired after the capability landed" for food/water/speed).
S14 (halving): remove the minimum-1 exception from effectiveHpMax (state/exhaustion.ts): halve uniformly with the SRD round-down rule (floor). When the clamp in adjust_exhaustion brings current HP to 0, apply the existing 0-HP lifecycle instead of a silent write: character → dying through the hpLifecycle path (do not invent instant death); combatant → through updateCombatant with the negative hpDelta (monster rules → dead, player-character rules → dying). Replace the min-1 test with the uniform-halving boundary test (1, odd, even maxima; character and combatant) asserting the resulting lifecycle.
S15 (retained gap evidence): buildRuleDispositionReport gains an optional injected gap registry parameter (default ENGINE_CAPABILITY_GAPS). Keep the real-pack empty-registry assertion and add a fixture test that drives one limit with a registered fixture gap through the real report producer, asserting operation, ownerBead, findingId, and the blocking-capability-gap unresolved-work entry — so removing the projection fails the test.

Map every finding to its tests in your completion notes.
acceptance_criteria: All listed findings repaired with the listed tests; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report mapping findings to tests in bd notes; bead closed by the child.
